prompt: Match each case to its cell of the table.
hint: Far or close; right or wrong.

pairs.left: A total of R$ 118.50 whose lines add to R$ 11.85
A total of R$ 2,721.50 whose lines add to R$ 272.15

prompt: Which half of outlier work is statistics?

choices.text: Deciding which values are wrong
choices.why: No statistic says what is true.

choices.text: Both halves, if the sample is large enough
choices.why: Size does not turn a distance into a verdict.

choices.text: Neither: outliers are a matter of opinion
choices.why: Flagging is measurable; deciding is evidence, not opinion.

choices.text: Flagging what is far
choices.why: Right; deciding needs the record, the context and people.

prompt: Lesson 2's summary of the totals gave Q1 = 32.70 and Q3 = 106.50. Where is the IQR fence for those quartiles? Give two decimal places.
Why does the z-score flag only 25 orders when the IQR fence flags 2,488?
hint: What are the extremes doing to the standard deviation?

choices.text: The z-score uses the median, which ignores extremes
choices.why: That is the robust z-score; the plain one uses the mean.

choices.text: The outliers inflate the spread it is measured in
choices.why: Right: masked by what it is looking for.

choices.text: The z-score only looks at delivered orders
choices.why: It ran on every order.

choices.text: A threshold of 3 is far stricter than one and a half
choices.why: The thresholds are in different units; the inflation is the cause.

prompt: What does the robust z-score replace the mean and standard deviation with?
hint: Neither moves when the extremes do.

choices.text: The median and the MAD
choices.why: Right, the MAD scaled by 1.4826.

choices.text: The mode and the range
choices.why: The range is set by the extremes.

choices.text: The mean of the middle half and Q3
choices.why: Not a standard pair.

choices.text: The median and the standard deviation
choices.why: Half robust: the spread would still move.

prompt: Every corporate order is beyond both the IQR fence and the z-score line. What does that show about the rules?

choices.text: Both rules are broken and should not be used
choices.why: They did their job: they found what is far.

choices.text: Corporate orders must be removed before any analysis
choices.why: They are real revenue; they need a label.

choices.text: They decide what to look at, never what is true
choices.why: Right: real orders are flagged and some typos are not.

choices.text: The rules agree, so the flagged orders are errors
choices.why: Agreement on distance says nothing about truth.

prompt: Order 122133 has a total of R$ 118.50 and lines adding to R$ 11.85. Which check found it?

choices.text: The IQR fence
choices.why: R$ 118.50 is below the fence.

choices.text: The z-score
choices.why: Far below its line.

choices.text: The robust z-score
choices.why: It sits near the middle of the distribution.

choices.text: The total against its own lines
choices.why: Right; no distance rule would ever look at it.

prompt: Every typed total was what multiple of its lines?
When a total and its lines disagree, why trust the lines?
hint: Which is harder to mistype consistently?

choices.text: Seven lines resist a consistent slip
choices.why: Right, and here every disagreement is exactly a factor of ten.

choices.text: Lines are always entered by the customer
choices.why: Who enters them is not the argument.

choices.text: Totals are computed later and lines are stored first
choices.why: Order of storage proves nothing here.

choices.text: The database marks totals as less reliable
choices.why: No such mark exists.

prompt: The sixteen corporate orders are real. What do they need?
hint: Some questions want them and some do not.

choices.text: A label saying what they are
choices.why: Right: each report chooses.

choices.text: Deletion before any report
choices.why: They are real revenue.

choices.text: Correction to a typical order size
choices.why: Their totals are right.

choices.text: Nothing, since they are correct
choices.why: Unlabelled, they quietly distort the household figures.

prompt: For which questions should the corporate orders be kept in? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: Total revenue for 2025
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: The typical household basket
choices.why: No: one clinic moves the average.

choices.text: December's revenue, with the corporate share stated
choices.why: Yes, said out loud.

choices.text: A campaign aimed at families
choices.why: No.

prompt: Why did no outlier rule on order totals find the refund account?
hint: Look at each of its orders.

choices.text: Refunded orders have no total
choices.why: They keep their totals.

choices.text: The account's orders were all below R$ 50
choices.why: Their size was ordinary, not tiny.

choices.text: Only the per-customer pattern is odd
choices.why: Right: choose the unit, then summarise.

choices.text: The rules only run on delivered orders
choices.why: They ran on every order.

prompt: How many orders did customer C01857 place, all refunded?
hint: The first row of the table.

prompt: What is the analyst's job with the refund account?
hint: Who decides whether it is fraud?

choices.text: Delete the account and its orders from the data
choices.why: That destroys the evidence and the revenue history.

choices.text: Report it, with the evidence
choices.why: Right; the fraud team decides.

choices.text: Block the customer from ordering again
choices.why: Not an analyst's action, and not proven.

choices.text: Nothing: refunds are the payments team's business
choices.why: Detection is exactly the analyst's part.

prompt: How many order lines charged sugar at R$ 134.90?
Why did lesson 7's consistency check not find the sugar price?

choices.text: The check ignores products sold by the unit
choices.why: Every line counts.

choices.text: Sugar orders were refunded
choices.why: They were delivered and charged.

choices.text: The check was only run on December
choices.why: It ran on the whole year.

choices.text: The error is upstream of both lines and totals
choices.why: Right: a reference typo is copied consistently.

prompt: Why is the sugar price not corrected in the analysis?
hint: What money did the company receive?

choices.text: The old price might be the typo
choices.why: Twelve-ninety for a kilo of sugar matches every other month.

choices.text: It was charged: the business decides
choices.why: Right: report it to buyers and finance.

choices.text: Prices are never cleaned, only quantities
choices.why: No such rule.

choices.text: 510 lines are too few to matter
choices.why: R$ 115,412.00 matters.

prompt: Why is setting the 137 negative totals to zero safe?
hint: Where does the zero come from?

choices.text: Payments confirm zero is what was charged
choices.why: Right; it is a fact, not an estimate.

choices.text: Zero is the median of the negative values
choices.why: The median of negatives is negative.

choices.text: Negative values cannot be stored in pandas
choices.why: They can.

choices.text: The coupons were cancelled afterwards
choices.why: Nothing says so.

prompt: Where does the fix for future negative totals belong?

choices.text: In every report that reads the orders
choices.why: That treats the symptom each time.

choices.text: In the payment gateway
choices.why: It already charges zero correctly.

choices.text: In the website's checkout
choices.why: Right: cap the coupon at the basket's value.

choices.text: In the customer file
choices.why: Customers do not cause it.

prompt: The decisions moved revenue and the mean, but the median stayed at R$ 57.60. Why?

choices.text: The median was computed before the decisions
choices.why: It was computed both times.

choices.text: Only seven orders changed
choices.why: A hundred and forty-four changed; their place is what matters.

choices.text: The median cannot change after cleaning
choices.why: It can, if the middle changes.

choices.text: The changes sat at the ends
choices.why: Right.

prompt: Put the handling of a flagged value in order.
items: Flag what is far, or inconsistent
Look for the explanation in the record and its context
Decide: correct, keep, set aside or report
Write the decision as a flag in the data
trap: Deciding before looking turns the clinic's order into a deletion.

prompt: A delivery van's fuel log shows one refuel of 900 litres in a van with an 80-litre tank. What kind of case is it?

choices.text: A real event, like the corporate orders
choices.why: No tank holds it.

choices.text: A pattern across refuels, like the refunds
choices.why: One value is enough to see this one.

choices.text: An impossible value: a domain rule rules it out
choices.why: Right; find the cause, perhaps a decimal point lost from 90.0.

choices.text: Fine, since it is within three standard deviations
choices.why: Distance is irrelevant when the value cannot exist.
